rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Male semen is secreted in the testes, passes through fine ducts to the seminal vesicles, then travels through the spermatic and ejaculatory passages.
rows.anchor: Meni husyelerde ifraz olunup ev‘iye-i âtiye denilen ev‘iye-i mahsûsasından te‘âkub üzere geçer, habl-i menevî kanât-ı nâkılesinden havsalaya gider

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Female fluid is a light, transparent, pure secretion from the vaginal walls and nearby labia; Elmalılı says it lacks the life present in male semen.
rows.anchor: Dişinin suyu; evvelâ biraz lüzûceti bulunan bir sâil-i mâyi‘dir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God designed the female passages so that fluid release brings pleasure and awakens her reproductive organs for fertilization of the ovum.
rows.anchor: kudret-i ilâhiye fevhe-i fercde o ev‘iye-i intısâbiyeyi yaratmış ve bu sâilin nüzûlünü tam bir lezzet ile müterâfık kılmıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paired ovaries resemble the male testes and contain small follicles with viscous fluid, which Elmalılı cautiously identifies as embryonic seeds.
rows.anchor: Sâniyen, erkekteki husyeler menzilesinde olan hacimleri fındık gibi ve hey’etleri lîfî, basık beyzî şekilde bulunan iki mebîz dahi lüzûcetli bir sâili muhtevî

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fallopian tubes attach to the uterus, surround the ovaries with their fringed ends, and carry the ovarian material toward the womb.
rows.anchor: Rahimin iki cânibi üzerinde a‘lâdan her biri bir cânibde iki sakbe vardır. Bunlara rahim boruları denilen iki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı describes the ovarian follicles as preformed seeds capable of later growth through male semen; the tubes convey them to the womb.
rows.anchor: bilâhare erkek menisinden nümüvvü kābil olmak üzere önce tekvin olunmuş birer bezr diye zan ve telakkī olunmaktadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This account accords with juristic descriptions: male semen is white, thick, and spurting, while female fluid is thin, yellow, and non-spurting.
rows.anchor: fıkıhta erkek menisi beyaz, galîz ve dıfıklı, kadın menisi rakīk, sarı ve dıfıksız olur diye târif olunması da bu îzâhât ile mütenâsibdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The child comes from the two fluids issuing between loins and breastbones; Elmalılı says the female contributes a vessel-like element.
rows.anchor: Bu suretle veled, sulb ile terâib arasından çıkan iki suyun mecmû‘undan husûle gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Male spurting semen contains many sperm cells; each, after growth, may develop into a world-like being and generate the nervous system.
rows.anchor: Erkeğin dâfik olan menisi birçok miktarda habbât-ı meneviyeyi ihtivâ eyler ki her biri nümüvvünden sonra neş’et ettiği kâine şebîh kâinat olmak mümkin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human development proceeds from the nutfa to the alaqa, an attached drop, then to a morsel, bones, flesh, and a seventh stage of renewed creation before birth.
rows.anchor: İnsan bu vechile nutfe mertebesinden üçüncü mertebe olan aleka tavrına geçer ki o tutmuş olan nutfe olup cidden muhtelif zamanlarda

rows.speaker: Ulemâ
rows.claim: Scholars hold that the dark original point in the transparent embryonic fluid adheres to its membranes.
rows.anchor: bu nokta ulemânın re’yine göre lifaflarına mültesıktır

rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: Others place the dark original point in the middle of the fluid rather than attached to its membranes.
rows.anchor: Bazılarının re’yince ise o sâilin vasatında sâbihtir

rows.speaker: Bukrat
rows.claim: Hippocrates says that after six days a small transparent sphere forms in the fluid.
rows.anchor: Bukrat altı günde sâilin vasatında şeffaf bir küre-i sağīre olur demiş

rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: Some say the embryonic form can be observed only after fifteen days.
rows.anchor: bazıları da ancak on beş günden sonra müşahede olunabileceğini söylemiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says implantation takes some days, but the duration has not been established across animal species; reports give rabbits three days and dogs six to eight.
rows.anchor: Zâhir olan tavşanda üç gün, köpeklerde altıdan yediye

rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: Some say the human form begins after thirty-five days, when it is about the size of a bee; Elmalılı notes that other accounts exist.
rows.anchor: bazıları ceninde şekl-i beşerînin ancak otuz beş günde başladığına

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reproductive organs are intricately arranged in concealed, protected places to perform their vital functions; the wording points to this arrangement.
rows.anchor: min tarafillah itkān üzere yapılıp mestur ve mahfuz mevzi‘lerde müretteben gereği gibi yerleştirilmiş olan tenasül cihazlarına

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coordinated reproductive and neural functions point to God’s power and guardianship over the human self, recalling the primordial testimony of Adam’s descendants.
rows.anchor: nefs-i müdrikenin irâdî ve gayr-i irâdî hükmü arasında cereyan eylediğine ve binâen‘aleyh bundan hilkat-i beşerin mütalaasıyla

rows.speaker: بعض المُلحدين
rows.claim: As Razi reports, some atheists object that semen is produced from the residue of digestion and draws qualities from all bodily organs, so it cannot originate only between loins and breastbones.
rows.anchor: Râzî’nin naklettiği vechile burada bazı mülhidler Kur’an’da böyle mâ-i dâfikten bahsedilerek

rows.speaker: بعض المُلحدين
rows.claim: They argue that if the phrase means the most important semen components form there, this is false because the brain develops them; they cite resemblance to the brain and eye weakness after excess ejaculation.
rows.anchor: Râzî’nin naklettiği vechile burada bazı mülhidler Kur’an’da böyle mâ-i dâfikten bahsedilerek

rows.speaker: بعض المُلحدين
rows.claim: They argue the phrase cannot mean semen is stored there, since its repository is the seminal vessels, which they say are folded together from the testicles onward.
rows.anchor: Râzî’nin naklettiği vechile burada bazı mülhidler Kur’an’da böyle mâ-i dâfikten bahsedilerek

rows.speaker: بعض المُلحدين
rows.claim: They also reject the phrase if it means the point of semen’s exit, arguing that sensory evidence shows it does not emerge from there.
rows.anchor: Râzî’nin naklettiği vechile burada bazı mülhidler Kur’an’da böyle mâ-i dâfikten bahsedilerek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı rejects these arguments as conjectural sophistry and says divine speech is more worthy of adherence than guesses about semen’s production, separation, or organs’ contributions.
rows.anchor: Yukarıki îzâhâttan sonra bu itirazların bi-gayri hak söylenmiş safsatalardan ibaret olduğunu anlamak kolay olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reads “between loins and breastbones” as a comprehensive, figurative expression embracing the viscera, reproductive organs, nerves, the whole body, and intercourse.
rows.anchor: hakikat ve kinayesiyle bütün ahşâyı ve tenasül cihazlarını ihtivâ ve sinirleri hatta bütün bedeni

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pure semen forms and is stored in the seminal vesicle connected to the loins; during intercourse, its passage from the woman’s vulva toward the womb occurs between her loins and breastbones.
rows.anchor: meninin hâlis meni olarak tevellüd ve infisâli ve müstekarrı sulbe bağlı olan havsala-i meniye müntehîdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fluid is specifically called “spurting” because its emission and point of passage during intercourse depend on the region between the woman’s loins and breastbones.
rows.anchor: Onun için burada da “mâ-i dâfik” mutlak bırakılmayıp bu şarta işaret için bu sıfatla tavsif olunmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All organs participate in this function, especially the brain; the loins support the spinal cord, while the front neck, chest, and breastbones also support nerve structures.
rows.anchor: Arkada sulb, dimağdan gelen nuhâ‘-i şevkînin kal‘ası olduğu gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase also expresses instinctive desire, which continually awakens in animals and directs them to meet their needs.
rows.anchor: Bu vechile sinir teşekkülâtının mesnedi olan sulb ile terâib arası bir de her hayvanda dâima mütenebbih olan ve ihtiyâcâtının

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sensory stimuli reach the brain, but the state of the viscera shapes perception and response; hunger can make food attractive, while a full stomach can cause indifference or disgust.
rows.anchor: aynı gıdayı nefis ihmal eder veya tiksinir de idrak merkezi o hayvanda onu teb‘îde mahsus hareketler ihdas eyler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Visceral effects spread through the whole nervous system at once; the dominant need governs behavior, as a hungry wolf attacks prey before a female.
rows.anchor: bu teessür yalnız kendisine ihtiyaç bulunan uzva in‘ikas etmekle kalmaz, cümle-i asabiyenin (sinir takımının) hepsine sirâyet eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Immediate animal actions, including those of newborn humans, arise from instinct; as the brain matures, self-awareness develops and visceral drives lose their former control.
rows.anchor: Zira yalnız bu kuvve-i ilhâmiyedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mature mental needs can exceed survival; they may sink into purposeless amusement and misuse, or seek spiritual perfection through self-sacrifice and service to God’s servants.
rows.anchor: Bu suretle hayattan fedâkârlığı istilzam eden bu zihnî ihtiyaçlar ya kendinden başka gaye gözetmeyen abes, lehv ü la‘b zevkinden ibaret bir sukūt

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı associates empty religious play with the people described in 7:51 and 6:70, and spiritual aspiration with the sealed pure drink of 83:25–26.
rows.anchor: ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُوا۟ دِينَهُمْ لَهْوًۭا وَلَعِبًۭا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says God names the loins and breastbones because their connected neural branches participate in these instinctive and mental influences; critics miss the brain–nerve relation.
rows.anchor: Bu hikmet ile de Allah teâlâ sulb ü terâibi bilhassa zikir buyurmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attention to human creation from a drop helps people recognize themselves and the deliberate Creator, an especially evident proof of divine power.
rows.anchor: Bu vechile insanın nutfeden hilkatine nazar-ı dikkati celbetmenin fâidesi de pek büyüktür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The body’s extraordinary composition and the transformation of a lowly substance like mucus into a rational, remembering, aspiring human prove the Creator’s existence and power.
rows.anchor: insanın bedeninde terkîbât-ı acîbe ekserdir. Binâen‘aleyh onun sümük gibi hakir ve basit görünen bir maddeden halkı kādir-i muhtârın vücûduna ve kudretine edeldir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person knows their own condition better than other people’s, so reflection on their own creation is a more complete proof.
rows.anchor: İnsanın kendi ahvâline ıttılâ‘ı başkalarının ahvâline ıttılâ‘dan ekserdir. Onun için bu, delâlette daha etemdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People continually observe birth in their children and other animals, making this evidence for the deliberate Creator especially strong.
rows.anchor: İnsanın bu ahvâli hem evlâdında

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human creation also proves resurrection: the Creator gathers scattered components, forms them, and breathes in a soul, so He can gather them again after death.
rows.anchor: mevt ile o eczânın teferrukundan sonra onları cem‘e ve evvelki gibi düzgün mahluklar yapmaya kādir olduğunu itiraf elbette vâcib olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Creator who first formed the human being can return him through death and resurrection, bringing him before God and making Himself known.
rows.anchor: Şüphesiz o yaradan o insanı döndürmeye elbette kādirdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This return expresses the Qur’anic teaching that people return to God, which Elmalılı connects to 2:245, 10:56, 11:34, 28:70–88, 36:22–83, 41:21, and 43:85.
rows.anchor: mazmûnunu ifade eden bu ircâ‘insanın Sûre-i Mü’minûn’da zikrolunan dokuz tavrından

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı identifies the return as the eighth and ninth of the nine human stages in al-Mu’minun: death followed by resurrection on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: insanın Sûre-i Mü’minûn’da zikrolunan dokuz tavrından sekizinci ve dokuzuncu mertebe olarak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sarā’ir is the plural of sarīra: hidden beliefs, intentions, loves, resentments, motives, and secret good or evil deeds.
rows.anchor: “Serâir” “serîre”nin cem‘idir ki kalblerde gizlenen

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Testing the secrets means exposing and examining them to distinguish the good from evil and the pure from the filthy.
rows.anchor: pisini temizini ayırmak için izhar

rows.speaker: بعض الأحاديث
rows.claim: Some hadiths name faith in divine unity, fasting, prayer, alms, and washing after major ritual impurity as the “secrets” tested on that day.
rows.anchor: “tevhid, savm, salât, zekât, cenâbetten gusül Allah teâlâ’nın يَوْمَ تُبْلَى ٱلسَّرَآئِرُ buyurduğu serâirdir” diye vârid olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These acts qualify because their validity depends on inward assent and intention, and—apart from faith—because they are devotional acts; the report gives examples, not an exhaustive restriction.
rows.anchor: Bunların serâir olmasında iki vecih vardır. Birisi bunların sıhhati sırf umûr-ı kalbiyeden olan tasdîke ve niyete mütevakkıf olmasıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse cannot be restricted to these good practices: it includes all secrets, especially vile hidden matters whose exposure is a severe warning.
rows.anchor: âyetteki “serâir” iyi ve kötü bütün serâire âm u şâmil olduğu ve zuhûrundan korkulacak serâir-i habîseye şümûlü hasebiyle

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Hasan al-Basri rebuked the poet Ahwas for claiming that his hidden love would remain secret on the day when secrets are exposed.
rows.anchor: Hasan-ı Basrî Hazretleri şair Ahvas’ın: سَيَبْقَى لَهَا فِي مُضْمَرِ الْقَلْبِ وَالْحَشَا سَرِيرَةُ وُدٍّ يَوْمَ تُبْلَى السَّرَائِرُ beytini işittiği zaman

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Hasan’s response was, “How heedless he was of ‘By the heaven and the night visitor’!”
rows.anchor: “Ve’s-semâi ve’t-târıktan ne kadar gaflet etmiş!” diye şâiri

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The day when secrets are tested” modifies the return, not “is able”; God’s power is unrestricted by that day, so Elmalılı prefers treating it as a new sentence.
rows.anchor: Bu yevm ilk nazarda zannedilebileceği gibi “kādir”in zarfı değil, “rec‘”e müte‘alliktir, çünkü kudret o gün ile mukayyed değil

words: فَمَا لَهُۥ مِن قُوَّةٍۢ وَلَا نَاصِرٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that day a person will have neither personal strength nor an outside helper to defend against God or keep secrets concealed.
rows.anchor: o insan için ne bir kuvvet vardır ne de bir nâsır

words: فَمَا لَهُۥ مِن قُوَّةٍۢ وَلَا نَاصِرٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No helper can oppose God because sovereignty on that day belongs to Him, as 22:56 states.
rows.anchor: Çünkü ٱلْمُلْكُ يَوْمَئِذٍۢ لِّلَّهِ’dır

words: فَمَا لَهُۥ مِن قُوَّةٍۢ وَلَا نَاصِرٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those whose secrets are pure will be fortunate before God; those exposed as vile face painful punishment, when wealth and children avail nothing except for one who comes with a sound heart.
rows.anchor: O gün يَنْفَعُ مَالٌ يَوْمَ لَاَ وَلَاَ بَنُونَ. اِلَاَّ مَنْ اَتَى اللّٰهَّٰ بِقَلْبٍ سَل۪يمٍ’dir

words: فَمَا لَهُۥ مِن قُوَّةٍۢ وَلَا نَاصِرٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should reflect on their humble origin, avoid misusing their God-given power or surrendering to base impulses, remember God’s watchfulness, and strive to meet Him with a sound heart, faith, and good works.
rows.anchor: Onun için insan neden yaratıldığına bakmalı da sulb ile terâib arası gibi bir kafes, bir geçit olan dünyada Hâlık’ın kendisine verdiği kuvveti sû’-i isti‘mâl etmemeli
